issues.title: T-003: Group commits into release-note sections
issues.body:
Ticket file: `tickets/T-003-group-commits-into-sections.md` (https://github.com/UBayouski/tracenotes/blob/main/tickets/T-003-group-commits-into-sections.md). The ticket file is the specification; this issue mirrors it.

**Goal.** Turn a list of parsed commits into the sections a release note is made of, with every entry carrying its source and every input commit accounted for.

**Input.** `LoggedCommit[]` as produced by `parseGitLog` (T-002, `src/gitlog.ts`).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `groupCommits(commits: LoggedCommit[]): ReleaseGroups` returns `sections: Section[]` in this fixed order, omitting empty sections: `Breaking changes`, `Features` (type `feat`), `Bug fixes` (`fix`), `Performance` (`perf`), `Reverts` (`revert`), then one section per remaining conventional type in alphabetical order titled by the type name (`build`, `chore`, `ci`, `docs`, `refactor`, `style`, `test`, and any other type), then `Unclassified` for non-conventional messages.
2. Every entry has `sha` (40 hex), `shortSha` (first 7), `subject`, `scope` (or null), `prNumber` (or null), `issueRefs`, `breaking`, and `type` (or null). An entry without `sha` is impossible by construction (No Orphan Notes).
3. A commit appears in exactly one section. A breaking commit goes to `Breaking changes` with its `breakingNotes` attached and does not also appear under its type.
4. Merge commits (subject starts with `Merge `) are not placed in a section. They are returned in `ignored: IgnoredEntry[]` with `reason: "merge commit"` and the same entry fields.
5. `total` equals `commits.length`, and the sum of all section entry counts plus `ignored.length` equals `total` (Nothing Vanishes). This is checked by a test on every fixture.
6. Order inside a section is the input order.
7. Entries are plain data, no functions, so the result can be serialized with `JSON.stringify` unchanged.
8. CLI: `node src/cli.ts group` reads a git log stream from stdin (same contract as `log`) and prints `ReleaseGroups` as JSON. Exit 0 when the stream parses, including when `malformed` records exist; those are passed through as `malformed` in the output so they stay visible. Exit 2 on empty stdin, and the same terminal-stdin behavior as `log` (T-026).
9. Edge cases covered by tests: a stream containing only merge commits (no sections, all ignored, totals match); a `feat!` commit with no `BREAKING CHANGE` footer (lands in `Breaking changes` with an empty notes list); a type never seen before such as `wip` (gets its own section, not dropped).

## Out of scope

Markdown rendering (T-004), version calculation (T-005), configurable section names and ignore patterns (T-008), source links as URLs (T-010).

## Verification

`npm run check`. Tests in `tests/group.test.ts` driven by `tests/fixtures/log-basic.bin` plus inline streams for the edge cases. CLI behavior tested as a child process in `tests/cli.test.ts`. AGENTS.md rule 6 applies: validate fields on raw text, no trim-then-validate.

## Definition of done

- Branch `agent/issue-<n>-...` with one Conventional Commits commit referencing this issue.
- Final comment lists each criterion as met or not met with the proving test.
- Qodo review read and confirmed findings fixed. A human opens the PR and merges.

issues.title: T-026: Print usage instead of blocking when stdin is a terminal
issues.body:
Ticket file: `tickets/T-026-usage-when-stdin-is-a-terminal.md` (https://github.com/UBayouski/tracenotes/blob/main/tickets/T-026-usage-when-stdin-is-a-terminal.md). The ticket file is the specification; this issue mirrors it.

**Goal.** `tracenotes parse` and `tracenotes log` must not hang waiting for input when a user runs them in a terminal with no argument and no pipe. Carried forward from the Day 1 and Day 3 journals.

**Context.** Today `readStdin()` in `src/cli.ts` awaits `process.stdin` unconditionally. In an interactive shell that blocks until Ctrl-D, with no hint of what went wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When `parse` has no message argument and stdin is a terminal (`process.stdin.isTTY === true`), the CLI prints a one-line error (`error: no commit message given and stdin is a terminal`) followed by the usage text to stderr, and exits 2 without reading stdin.
2. When `log` is run and stdin is a terminal, same behavior with `error: no git log stream on stdin (stdin is a terminal)`.
3. Piped and redirected stdin keep working exactly as before: every existing test in `tests/cli.test.ts` passes unchanged.
4. `parse <message>` with an argument never consults stdin, TTY or not.
5. `main(argv, io?)` accepts an optional `io` object `{ stdinIsTTY: boolean, readStdin: () => Promise<string> }` so the TTY branch is testable without a pseudo-terminal. The default `io` reads the real process. No other module gains access to process streams (AGENTS.md: process output stays in `cli.ts`).
6. Tests: one test each for criteria 1, 2 and 4 using an injected `io`; criterion 3 is covered by the existing child-process tests; one new child-process test confirms piped stdin still parses.
7. `USAGE` text says that `parse` and `log` read stdin only when it is not a terminal.

## Out of scope

Interactive prompting, reading a message from an editor, Windows console specifics beyond `isTTY`.

## Verification

`npm run check` passes. Manual: `node src/cli.ts log` in a terminal returns immediately with exit code 2; `git log --format='%H%x1f%an%x1f%aI%x1f%B%x1e' -3 | node src/cli.ts log` still prints JSON.

## Definition of done

- Branch `agent/issue-<n>-...` with one Conventional Commits commit referencing this issue.
- PR body lists each criterion as met or not met with the proving test.
- Qodo review read and confirmed findings fixed. A human merges.
